name: Vedis
tagline: Embeddable C datastore with 70+ Redis-like commands and a single-file ACID key-value store.
description: Vedis is a self-contained C library from Symisc Systems that implements more than 70 commands modelled on Redis, but runs inside your process with no network layer. Data lives in one cross-platform disk file (or in memory) managed by a transactional key-value engine shared with its sibling UnQLite, and the command interface can be extended with your own C functions. That makes it handy for embedded devices and desktop apps that want Redis-style hashes, sets and lists without running a server. The current public release is 1.2.6; repository activity has been limited to occasional fixes, the latest in 2021.
statusNote: Still distributed by Symisc (release 1.2.6), but the last code change was a bug fix in Nov 2021; UnQLite gets more attention.

scale.notes: Single database file; the vendor claims terabyte-sized databases are supported.

strengths: Redis-style data structures without a server process
Whole database in one portable file across 32/64-bit and endianness
Zero dependencies; amalgamated C source drops into any project
ACID transactions on the underlying key-value store
weaknesses: Sleepycat licence requires releasing source of software that redistributes it
Not wire-compatible with Redis; clients must link the library
useCases: Embedded devices needing structured key-value storage
Desktop apps wanting Redis-like semantics locally
notIdealFor: Closed-source products unwilling to meet Sleepycat terms
